messages:
alyssa-cs: Heads-up — scheduling a capacity bring-up + probe for Horizon next Wed 09:00 UTC. Need quick alignment on quota, autoscale headrooms, and a short customer enablement script. Renewal note: customer is watching latency numbers closely.
pranav-ops: 👍 on the slot. Do we have the final committed quota numbers from finance? I have the draft autoscale policy but want to ensure we don't oversubscribe.
marie-ml: FYI the model variant Horizon-3B-v2 is the one they'll use in prod. Perf profile: p50 ~ 85ms on 16k batch pipeline, but during burst it can hit 180-220ms unless batching is tuned.
jon-sre: Can we run a 30m smoke + 60m ramp to peak? I'll coordinate on-call and fallback routes. Also advise a canary route for the first 15 minutes.
alyssa-cs: Plan: 09:00 — smoke (30m), 09:30 — ramp (60m) to target QPS, 10:30 — steady 30m, then teardown. Target QPS = 240 rps (customer expected peak). Autoscale policy suggestion: min=4 pods, target_cpu=70%, scale_step=+2 pods, cooldown=60s.
pranav-ops: That scale policy looks reasonable. Need to ensure reserved GPUs >= anticipated pods at peak. I'll lock reserved capacity at 6 GPUs for the window. Also tagging for cost/chargeback: horizon-dedicated-jan-renew.
marie-ml: Small tweak: add KV cache priming for the first 10k sequences to avoid cold-kv spikes. We'll push a prefix-warm script.
vela-eng: I'll drop the KV priming script into the runbook. Script snippet for load generator:
```bash
# run generator
python -m loadgen --target 240 --duration 90 --p95_latency_target 300 --model Horizon-3B-v2
```
Include warmup flag: `--warm-prefix 10000`
alyssa-cs: Perfect. Who will own customer-facing enablement? I can do a 15-min runthrough with their infra lead at 08:30 UTC. Need a short checklist that covers: token limits, request routing, auth tokens, and what to do if latency > 400ms.
jon-sre: I'll produce a short runbook section for fallback: switch routing to small-variant Horizon-3B-quant (lower cost, slightly higher latencies) and apply rate-limit 20% for non-critical routes. I'll post the exact commands.
sre-bot: @channel Incident playbook template created: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/dedicated-fallback (auto-attached to thread).
pranav-ops: Quick question on quotas: are we mapping customer "committed_units" to GPU-hours or QPS? Finance prefers GPU-hours but ops runs QPS tests. We should record both.
alyssa-cs: We map committed_units -> reserved GPU-hours, and we publish an expected QPS envelope per GPU. I'll add both to the post-test summary for renewal stakeholders.
marie-ml: Post-test metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, batch sizes distribution, cache hit %, and error rate by route. We'll compare against the baseline perf profile.
vela-eng: Also capture tail-KV latencies — those explain sudden token spikes. I'll add a Graf panel.
alyssa-cs: OK owners: Pranav (capacity & quotas), Jon (oncall + fallback commands), Vela (runbook + dashboards), Marie (perf baselines & scripts), me (enablement + customer comms).
pranav-ops: I'll lock reserve, update autoscale policy in the infra repo, and post the terraform diff by EOD today.
jon-sre: I'll put an on-call rotation and pager for the window. If any 5xx spikes > 1% for 5m, trigger failover to fallback route.
marie-ml: Post-run: I'll run two prompt sets to check quality regressions and capture notable hallucinations for CS.
alyssa-cs: Customer note to include in invite: "We're running an ops-oriented capacity test next Wed — minimal risk to prod, can exercise autoscale and routing. We'll share the dashboard and a short 15min debrief afterwards." Anyone want to add wording?
pranav-ops: Add: "If you'd like any routes excluded from the test, tell us by Tue 12:00 UTC."
alyssa-cs: Good. Final ask: capture a single line renewal risk summary after the test: green/amber/red and the reason. We'll attach it to the QBR pack.
vela-eng: Added a post-test checkbox in the runbook for "renewal risk summary".
alyssa-cs: Thanks team — I'll send the calendar invite and customer enablement doc. Ping me if anything changes. :thumbsup:
